ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, from left to right, there are six gray shapes drawn inside square frames of the same size. The 1st is an L shape composed of the left side and the bottom side; the 2nd is an H shape with two vertical sides plus a middle horizontal bar; the 3rd is a U shape with two vertical sides plus the bottom side; the 4th is a stair/zigzag-shaped gray figure; the 5th is a T shape with an upper horizontal bar plus a middle vertical bar; the 6th is a cross/plus-sign shape. Reasoning: What is being compared is the perimeter of each gray figure and the perimeter of the original complete square paper. If a white rectangle is cut away from a corner of the square, the two lengths removed from the outer boundary will be replaced by two equal-length sides of the new internal boundary, so the perimeter does not change. If a white notch is cut into the middle of one side, then two vertical or horizontal inner walls will be added, and the perimeter becomes larger. The 1st L shape has only one corner notch, so the perimeter is the same; the 2nd H shape has upper and lower middle notches, so the perimeter becomes larger; the 3rd U shape has a middle notch on the upper side, so the perimeter becomes larger; the 4th stair shape can be regarded as a corner notch, so the perimeter is the same; the 5th T shape has two bottom corner notches, so the perimeter is the same; the 6th plus-sign shape has four corner notches, so the perimeter is the same. Therefore, there are altogether 4 figures whose perimeters are equal to the perimeter of the original square paper.

raw_record.question_text: Maria has six equally big square pieces of plain paper. On each piece of paper she draws one of the figures shown below. How many of these figures have the same perimeter as the plain piece of paper itself?

method.method_draft: First describe the six grey figures from left to right in the image: an L-shape, an H-shape, a U-shape, a stepped/zigzag shape, a T-shape, and a plus-shape, all drawn inside equal square outlines. Use the text to know the comparison target: the perimeter of each grey figure versus the perimeter of the original plain square. Reason by starting with the full square perimeter. A white cutout taken from a corner does not change the perimeter, because the two removed outer boundary segments are replaced by two equal inner boundary segments. A white notch cut from the middle of a side increases the perimeter, because it adds two extra side walls without removing matching boundary length. Apply this to each figure: the L-shape has one corner cutout, so same perimeter; the H-shape has top and bottom middle notches, so larger perimeter; the U-shape has a middle top notch, so larger perimeter; the stepped shape has corner cutouts, so same perimeter; the T-shape has two bottom corner cutouts, so same perimeter; the plus-shape has four corner cutouts, so same perimeter. Count the matching figures: 4.
